claims.text: The uncoated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a robust caloric response near its transition temperature under magnetic fields.
The uncoated alloy has a robust caloric response near its transition temperature under pressure fields.
The uncoated alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack under cyclic mechanical and operational loads.
A 150 nm TiN coating can be deposited on the alloy by PVD at a substrate temperature below 500 °C under high vacuum.
The proposed PVD process is compatible with the bulk alloy.
The TiN coating will induce a compressive residual-stress layer at the alloy surface.
The coating-induced compressive surface stress will impede surface-crack nucleation.
The coating-induced compressive surface stress will impede crack propagation.
The 150 nm thickness is sufficiently small that the alloy's bulk caloric phase transformation will remain unaltered.
The TiN coating will improve the alloy's mechanical integrity and load-bearing capacity.
The TiN coating will significantly reduce surface cracking relative to the uncoated alloy.
The coated alloy will maintain the magnitude of its caloric response under applied magnetic fields.
The coated alloy will maintain the magnitude of its caloric response under applied pressure fields.
The coated alloy will maintain the sharpness of its caloric transition under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
The intervention is intended for cyclic magnetic- and pressure-field operation near the caloric transition temperature and under mechanical loads approaching the uncoated alloy's load-bearing limit.
Successful operation requires the TiN coating to remain stable and adherent under the specified cyclic conditions.
